# Differences from MSX-MUSIC BASIC Extension V2

> This is an English translation of the [Japanese original](../diff-from-mmbe.md). Where the two differ, the Japanese version is authoritative.

This document covers **the differences between MSX-AUDIO BASIC Extension Lite and its sibling [MSX-MUSIC BASIC Extension V2](../../msx-music/en/basic-reference.md) (hereafter V2)**
only. The full specification of the statements and MML is in [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md).

This BASIC extension is a port of V2 to the Y8950, and **their MML notation is almost the same**. A song written for V2 mostly plays as is once `CALL MUSIC` is changed to `CALL AUDIO`. Most of the differences come from the sound chips themselves.

| | V2 | This BASIC extension |
|---|---|---|
| Sound chip | MSX-MUSIC (OPLL / YM2413) | MSX-AUDIO (Y8950) / the Y8960's extended OPL2 part |
| FM | 9 voices (6 voices when the rhythm sounds are used) | Same |
| ADPCM | None | 1 voice |
| PSG | 3 voices (6 voices in the cartridge build, with the second set of SSGS added) | Same |
| Voices | Only one at a time for part of the library and for array voices | Independent per channel |
| Initialization | `CALL MUSIC` | `CALL AUDIO` |
| Decrease in memory available to BASIC | 965 bytes (1255 bytes in the cartridge build) | 2051 bytes (1328 bytes in the cartridge build) |

## How to initialize

```basic
CALL AUDIO(0, 0, 1, 1, 1)     ' corresponds to V2's CALL MUSIC(0, 0, 1, 1, 1)
```

The meaning of `<mode>` is broader. In V2 it is 0 (no rhythm) or 1 (with rhythm); here it is a bitmap of 0-7, where bit1 specifies whether there is a string for PCM and bit2 specifies the interrupt that times note lengths. **bit0 has the same meaning as in V2**, and unless bit2 is set, the tick source is also the same as in V2, so as long as only 0 and 1 are used, nothing needs to be rewritten.

| Bit | Meaning |
|---|---|
| bit0 | Uses the rhythm sounds |
| bit1 | The PLAY statement has a string for PCM |
| bit2 | Times note lengths with the sound chip's timer |

**The assignment used when the parameters are omitted is different.**

| | Default when omitted |
|---|---|
| V2 | `CALL MUSIC(1, 0, 1, 1, 1)` — 3 FM voices, one channel each |
| This BASIC extension | `CALL AUDIO(1, 0, 2, 2, 2)` — 6 FM voices, two channels each |

When two channels are assigned to one string, those two voices play the same notes in unison.
To use one voice per string, write `CALL AUDIO(1, 0, 1, 1, 1)`, as in V2.

Initialization also measures the size of the sound chip's sample RAM. If there is 32KB or more, voice file 0 starts out with the first 32KB
assigned to it ([ADPCM is available](#adpcm-is-available)).

Releasing with `CALL AUDIO(-1)` is the same as V2's `CALL MUSIC(-1)`. Only the amount of memory returned
to BASIC differs.

---

## Voices are independent per channel

**V2's tightest restriction is gone.** The OPLL shares its user voice registers among all channels, so in V2 the voices in the voice library without the `*` mark and the voices given in array variables **can only be held one at a time**.

```basic
CALL VOICE(@26, @27)   ' in V2, channel 1 also becomes voice 27
```

On the Y8950 each of the 9 channels has its own operator registers, so **whatever voices are lined up, and however many, all take effect**. The same applies when MML `@n` is written separately on each channel, and the voice library has no `*` distinction at all.

| Restriction in V2 | This BASIC extension |
|---|---|
| Voices without the `*` mark: only one at a time | No restriction |
| Voices marked `*` cannot be the source of `CALL VOICE COPY` unless mode 1 is set with `CALL VOICE MODE` | Any of 0-95 can be the source |
| Voice library of 64 voices | **The same 64 voices**. Numbers and names are unchanged |
| The destinations of `CALL VOICE COPY` are the five numbers 63, 64, 80, 96 and 112 | The 33 voices 63-95 |

---

## ADPCM is available

Of the PCM statements that give `Illegal function call` in V2, `SET PCM` and `COPY PCM` can be used.

```basic
CALL AUDIO(2, 0, 1, 1, 1)          ' set bit1 to have a string for PCM
CALL SET PCM(1, 4, 0, S%)          ' array S% as voice file 1
CALL COPY PCM(1, 0)                ' transfer to voice file 0 in sample RAM
PLAY#2, "CDE", "EFG", "GAB", "@0O5L4EFGA", ""
```

- ADPCM data is handled in units called **voice files** (0-15). The data itself can be placed in sample RAM, an array variable or VRAM
- Only what is placed in sample RAM can be played. Arrays and VRAM are transfer sources and destinations
- The MML for PCM is a subset of the MML for FM, and `@n` is the voice file number. `O5 E` is the pitch at exactly the sampling frequency given with `SET PCM`
- PCM does not use the FM channels, so the 9 FM voices are not reduced

`LOAD PCM` `SAVE PCM` `REC PCM` `PLAY PCM` `PCM FREQ` `PCM VOL` `CONVA` `CONVP` still give `Illegal function call`, as in V2.

## Tempo and note lengths

**The tick source can be chosen.** The default is the screen interrupt (VSYNC), the same as V2; setting bit2 of the `CALL AUDIO` mode switches it to the sound chip's timer.

| | V2 | This BASIC extension |
|---|---|---|
| Upper limit of lengths (`Ln` `Rn` `@Wn` `{ }n` and rhythm lengths) | 1-64 | **1-96** |
| Tick resolution | Fixed at 1 frame (16.7ms on NTSC) | Same when bit2=0. **48, 96 or 192 per quarter note when bit2=1** (decided by the tempo) |
| How tempo takes effect | Per channel | **One for the whole song** |

**The range that can be written in `Ln` is 1-96 regardless of the tick source.** With bit2=0, a fraction that cannot be expressed in whole ticks (a 96th note at T120 is 1.25 frames) is carried over to the next note so that the average comes out right. With bit2=1, a 96th note can be timed exactly at any tempo.

**However, with bit2=0, when `tempo × length` exceeds 14400, a note may not advance even one frame, and writing another note right after it gives `Illegal function call`** (T151 and above for `L96`; these figures are for NTSC, and on PAL 14400 becomes 12000). **V2 also has this property**; there the length limit is 64, so it is hit at T226 and above. Setting bit2=1 removes it (["Lengths that cannot be placed with VSYNC" in `basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md#lengths-that-cannot-be-placed-with-vsync)).

With bit2=1, the tick rate is rounded to the timer's resolution, so **it deviates by just under 1% from the time the tempo represents** (["Tempo" in `basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md#tempo)).

Whichever channel `Tn` is written on, it changes the tempo of all channels. To change the tempo partway through, write the same `T` in every string, both at the start and at the point of change (["Tempo" in `basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md#tempo)). In the next example, four eighth notes play at T120, and then it switches to T240.

```basic
PLAY#2, "T120L8CDEFT240GABC"
```

The tempo reaches the sound chip in playback order, so **`T` cannot be placed between the portamento `~` and the target note.** V2 allows it (`C4~T120E4`), but here it gives `Illegal function call`. Place `T` before `~`.

**With bit2=1, playback does not advance on a machine without the sound chip.** The screen interrupt that V2 uses arrives whether or not there is a sound chip, but bit2=1 uses the sound chip's own timer. Without the sound chip, `PLAY` returns, but the notes stay in the queue.

## Waveform selection in voice parameters

The voice parameters are 32 bytes, the same as V2, with the same layout. Only **offsets 21 and 29** have different bit assignments.

| Offset | V2 | This BASIC extension |
|--:|---|---|
| 21 | bit0: DM (modulator waveform; 0=sine wave, 1=half-wave rectified) | bit0-1: waveform selection |
| 29 | bit0: DC (carrier waveform) | bit0-1: waveform selection |

Here the waveform selection is 2 bits, choosing one of four waveforms per operator.
**On the Y8960's OPL2EX the waveform actually changes.** An MSX-AUDIO cartridge (Y8950) does not have this register; the write is dropped and the waveform stays a sine wave.

**This is asymmetric with V2.** V2's DM / DC are bit3 and bit4 of OPLL register 03H, and take effect even on a plain OPLL. The waveform selection here exists only on OPL2EX. The differences between the two chips are summarized in ["Sound chips" in `basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md#sound-chips).

Of the bits that V2 says "exist for compatibility with MSX-AUDIO and have no meaning in MSX-MUSIC", bit4-7 of offset 10 and the velocity sensitivity in 20 and 28 are ignored here as well. **The other two — bit0 of offset 10 (algorithm) and bit0-5 of offset 25 (carrier total level) — take effect here.** Voices in arrays made for V2 may sound different because of the values in these two.

All 64 presets in the voice library use waveform 0, so as long as the library is used, no difference appears.

## Panning of FM, PCM and rhythm

Both accept `In` in the FM, rhythm and PSG strings; only the sound part written to differs.

| String | V2 | This BASIC extension |
|---|---|---|
| For FM | Panning of the OPLLEX channels. The same value for all assigned channels | Panning of the OPL2EX channels. The same value for all assigned channels |
| For PCM | None | ADPCM panning of the OPL2EX |
| For rhythm | Panning of OPLLEX channels 7-9 | Panning of OPL2EX channels 7-9 |
| For PSG | SSGS panpot | Same |

The scale of n (1 is the far left, 128 the center, 255 the far right, and 0 is undefined) is the same. Here, panning moves only on the Y8960's OPL2EX; on an MSX-AUDIO cartridge (Y8950) the writes are ignored. For details, see ["Panpot with `I`" in `basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md#panpot-with-i).

## Things that touch registers

What `CALL AUDREG` and MML `Yr, d` write to is, naturally, the chip's registers, so the range is entirely different. `Y` written for V2's OPLL does not work as it is.

| | V2 (OPLL) | This BASIC extension (Y8950) |
|---|---|---|
| Registers | `00H`-`07H`, `0EH`-`18H`, `20H`-`28H`, `30H`-`38H`, `40H`-`48H`, `50H`-`58H` | `01H`-`12H`, `20H`-`35H`, `40H`-`55H`, `60H`-`75H`, `80H`-`95H`, `A0H`-`A8H`, `B0H`-`B8H`, `BDH`, `C0H`-`C8H`, `E0H`-`FFH` |
| Per channel | One user voice shared by all channels | Independent for each of the 9 channels |

**The range where the third-argument mask `Yr, d, m` takes effect is narrower.** Neither chip can read back the values written, so both keep a record of the current values; V2's record covers every register that `Y` accepts, whereas this one holds only `B0H`-`B8H` and `BDH`.

```basic
PLAY#2, "Y$B0,$20,$1F"   ' takes effect (sets only key-on)
PLAY#2, "Y$40,$10,$C0"   ' does not take effect; the whole register becomes 10H
```

`Yr, d, m` on PSG channels can read the PSG registers, so, as in V2,
the mask takes effect on every register.

---

## What V2 has and this one does not

**The OPLLEX ROM voice banks (`@65`-`@127` except 80, 96 and 112).** These are ROM preset voices of the Y8960's extended OPLL part, a feature of the OPLL side. `@n` on FM channels here accepts `@0`-`@95`, but `@64`-`@95` are user voices, not ROM presets. 96 and above give `Illegal function call`.

**`CALL VOICE MODE`.** It selects whether voices marked `*` play with the OPLL's built-in voices or with the library's parameters; the Y8950 has no built-in voices, so there is nothing that corresponds to it. Here it gives `Syntax error`.

**`CALL PCM PLAY` `CALL PCM REC` `CALL PAUSE`, for turbo R only.** Here they give `Syntax error`. ADPCM here plays, with MML, voice files defined with [`CALL SET PCM`](basic-reference.md#call-set-pcm).

## Handing over page 1 in the Y8960 cartridge build

The Y8960 cartridge build (`mabel_y8960.rom`) has statements that switch to another BASIC extension on the same cartridge. **`CALL MUSIC` is one of them, and is the statement that switches to V2.**

```basic
CALL AUDIO(0, 0, 1, 1, 1)
PLAY#2, "CDE"
CALL MUSIC                 ' V2 from here on
CALL MUSIC(0, 0, 1, 1, 1)  ' this (0,0,1,1,1) is read by V2
```

Before switching, the same cleanup as `CALL AUDIO(-1)` is done automatically, so playback stops, the memory returns to BASIC, and the voice file definitions in sample RAM are also lost.

[`CALL MIXER`](basic-reference.md#call-mixer), which sets the cartridge's hardware mixer, can also be used with the same syntax as in V2's cartridge build. It is also the same in that it can be used before `CALL AUDIO`, and that all six become 128 when switched in from another BASIC extension.

The standalone cartridge build (`mabel.rom`) does not have these statements.

Playing the second set of SSGS as three PLAY channels is also the same as in V2's cartridge build: `PLAY#1` is the PSG plus the second set, `PLAY#3` is `#2` plus the second set, and the register numbers for `Y` are `00H`-`0DH`, `10H`-`1DH` and the SSGS's own volume and panning (`20H`-`2EH`). The strings of `#3` are the `#2` sequence followed by three for the second set. `@V` (0-128) on PSG channels writing the SSGS channel volume is also the same. The standalone cartridge build (`mabel.rom`), like V2's replacement build, accepts these `Y` and `@V` and does nothing.

What differs is the timing of initialization: V2 returns the PSG panning to the center every time playback is stopped, and its cartridge build also returns the volume to 128, whereas this one returns them only at `CALL AUDIO`, and the values written with `@V` and `I` remain after stopping.

---

## What has not changed

The following can be written the same way as in V2.

| | |
|---|---|
| Statements | `CALL BGM` `CALL PITCH` `PLAY` `CALL PLAY` `CALL STOPM` `CALL TEMPER` `CALL TRANSPOSE` |
| MML extended in V2 | Length `0` and `R0`, pitch bend `P` / `@P`, portamento `~`, dotted rest `R.`, hexadecimal literal `$`, the PSG panpot `I`, `@W` `&` `{ }` on PSG, `Y` to PSG, PSG `@n` (tone/noise and envelope), and `R` inside a tuplet taking the tuplet length |
| MML for rhythm sounds | `B` `S` `M` `C` `H` `!` `Vn` `@An` and the length |
| Voice library | 64 voices. Numbers and names are both the same |
| Temperament | 0-21 of `CALL TEMPER` |

Portamento differs in one point: `T` cannot be placed between `~` and the target note ([Tempo and note lengths](#tempo-and-note-lengths)).

`CALL PITCH` and `CALL TRANSPOSE` also take effect the same way; only the pitch accuracy is higher (about ±2 cents in V2, about ±1 cent here).
